Billings dental exam cost: a published $99 new-patient cash special

Quick answer

Brewer Dental Center advertises a $99 new-patient cash special that includes a cleaning, dental examination and X-rays at its Billings offices. The practice says this special is for new, uninsured patients only, and it cannot be combined with dental insurance, other offers or reduced-fee plans. This is one clinic's published promotion, not a Billings-wide average, the lowest available price, or an independent guarantee of eligibility or appointments.

We have not verified a second Billings provider with a directly published comparable all-in new-patient price. Request written estimates from other local offices before drawing a price ranking. A promotional cleaning package is not an emergency-treatment quote or a quote for fillings, extractions, crowns, periodontal therapy or sedation.

If you need treatment beyond an exam

The cost and recovery expectations for treatment depend on diagnosis and procedure. A routine cleaning visit is different from managing an abscess, tooth extraction or oral surgery. Ask whether the office will examine an urgent problem at the promotional rate, what follow-up care might cost, and when an urgent infection or swelling needs immediate medical assessment. Do not delay urgent evaluation to chase a routine-care special.

Who may qualify for the cash special?

The advertised terms point to a new patient without dental insurance who is booking the described preventive-care visit. Call ahead if you have insurance, require a deep cleaning, have significant gum disease, or are booking for a child, because the offer does not specify every possible clinical exclusion. A clinician's examination determines appropriate treatment; a promotion should never dictate the care plan.

Five questions before scheduling

  1. Do I qualify for the $99 new-patient cash special at my preferred Billings location?
  2. Which type of cleaning is included, and what happens if periodontal treatment is recommended?
  3. Are the examination and all necessary X-rays included, or only certain images?
  4. What is the charge for any recommended treatment, and can I receive an itemized written plan?
  5. What are the cancellation terms and the earliest available appointment?

Red flags when comparing first-visit prices

  • A low headline fee that excludes required imaging or examination without saying so.
  • Pressure to accept irreversible treatment before getting a diagnosis and written estimate.
  • Claims that the cheapest promotional visit identifies the best dentist.
  • An inability to explain scope, insurance exclusions, or what changes if more treatment is required.

What a preventive visit bundle can and cannot tell you

A preventive exam, X-rays and routine cleaning are separate components of a first visit. The exam is the dentist's evaluation of the mouth, teeth, gums and any concerns you report. Images can help reveal issues that are not visible on the surfaces of the teeth. A routine cleaning removes deposits according to the clinical assessment. A single promotional fee may cover those named services, but it should never be taken to guarantee that no additional treatment will be recommended. If you already have pain, bleeding, a broken tooth or a known condition, tell the receptionist when scheduling so the appointment type matches the problem.

A quote for a standard cleaning is especially different from a treatment plan involving gum disease. Periodontal evaluation may reveal needs beyond routine preventive cleaning. The right question is not whether a more involved procedure is automatically necessary; it is what findings support the recommendation, whether the dentist can explain alternatives, and what each part costs. Ask for the tooth numbers, procedure names and any proposed sequence of visits in writing. You may seek a second opinion on non-emergency irreversible treatment.

Cash specials versus insurance benefits

Brewer's advertised cash offer excludes the use of dental insurance for that promotion. An insured patient should not assume that paying $99 in cash is the best choice, or that the insurer will reimburse that charge. A separate examination billed under the patient's insurance may involve deductibles, waiting periods, network status, frequency limits or no patient payment, depending on the plan. Before deciding, ask the office to estimate the in-network or out-of-network patient share for a comparable visit. Compare what is included, not just the advertised cash amount.

For people without insurance, ask whether the special must be paid in full on the visit date, whether any additional professional or facility charge exists, and what happens if clinical findings change the cleaning type. Membership programs, payment plans and promotional offers can have different terms; request those terms in writing if they are presented. A low introductory fee is useful only if the clinic can explain the price of any subsequent care without pressure to decide immediately.

What to ask about X-rays and records

The phrase “X-rays included” does not by itself specify which views will be taken. The dentist should decide which images are appropriate from examination, symptoms, age, risk factors and available prior records, while minimizing unnecessary radiation exposure. If you recently had dental images elsewhere, ask whether you can transfer them before the visit and whether they are diagnostically adequate for your concerns. Do not request imaging solely to maximize the apparent value of a promotion.

Ask for copies of your exam findings and images if you need a second opinion or are moving practices. Offices may have procedures for requesting copies and confirming identity. An explanation of whether a filling, extraction, periodontal procedure or specialist referral is needed should rest on clinical findings, not on a limited-time sales message.

When an urgent dental problem is not a routine new-patient visit

Swelling, fever, spreading facial redness, severe pain, trauma, or difficulty swallowing or breathing changes the decision. A preventive cleaning special is not an emergency response plan. Severe swelling with trouble breathing or swallowing needs emergency medical attention. For other urgent dental symptoms, call a dental office promptly and describe the problem clearly so staff can determine whether same-day assessment, imaging, treatment or referral is appropriate.

When calling about an urgent visit, ask separately for the examination fee, any imaging fee, and the estimate for possible same-day treatment. An office may be able to evaluate a problem without completing a cleaning, and there is no reason to assume a routine new-patient promotional package covers every urgent procedure. If the clinic cannot see you in a suitable timeframe, ask for an appropriate referral rather than waiting on a discounted preventive appointment.

Compare Billings practices on matching services

A useful apples-to-apples comparison records each practice's appointment type, eligibility restrictions, included examination, necessary imaging, cleaning category, clinician and office location, expected total, cancellation terms and follow-up process. For an insured patient, include network status and estimated patient responsibility. For an uninsured patient, include the cash total and whether any separately required consultation or procedure is excluded. If a clinic gives only a starting figure, mark the all-in amount as unknown rather than treating it as a competing fixed quote.

Our inclusion threshold for a published price is a named local office and a publicly accessible offer with identifiable restrictions. This guide has one such verified offer; it is not an exhaustive provider list. The absence of another publicly posted price does not mean another Billings dentist is more expensive, less qualified or unavailable. Call the offices you are genuinely considering and verify both prices and clinical fit.

How to verify and compare

Check Brewer's official offer page and call the practice for current terms, then compare other Billings offices by the same service bundle and complete expected charges.
